summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebrovascular accidents with aphasia and contractures, dysphagia, and chronic constipation was admitted for lethargy and found to be in septic shock. Initial evaluation revealed MRSA pneumonia and Clostridioides difficile infection as sources. He was intubated for airway protection but extubated the following day as his mental status returned to baseline. He required vasopressor support briefly, which was discontinued as hemodynamics stabilized. Acute kidney injury secondary to hypotension resolved with fluid resuscitation. Antibiotics were narrowed to vancomycin for both MRSA and C. diff. His bowel regimen was adjusted, and psychiatric medications were changed to improve safety. He was discharged to extended care on continued IV and oral vancomycin, with stable vital signs, improved mentation, and tolerance of enteral feeds.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
